transfer_points.heading: A valid out-of-state license
transfer_points.label: Licensing handbook
transfer_points.text: A valid license that has not expired can be transferred. The handbook still requires a vision screening, a short alcohol awareness course, surrender of the out-of-state license, and the same identity documents a first-time applicant brings. A motorcycle endorsement can transfer for an added fee. The new-resident section does not print that fee, so it is not guessed here.

transfer_points.heading: Expired, missing, or suspended licenses
transfer_points.label: Licensing handbook
transfer_points.text: If the out-of-state license has expired, the handbook says you take the examinations required of a first-time applicant. If you cannot hand over the old license, a certified driving record from the prior state is what the handbook requires in order to waive testing. A license that is suspended or revoked in another state blocks a West Virginia license until there is a clearance from the Problem Driver Point System. The handbook says it is illegal to drive in West Virginia on a suspended or revoked license from any state.

transfer_points.heading: A later address change
transfer_points.label: Licensing handbook
transfer_points.text: If you later change your address inside West Virginia, the handbook says you must tell the DMV in writing within 20 days. That clock is not the 30 days to get the license after you move in.

real_id_summary: A Wisconsin REAL ID is optional. There is no additional fee to upgrade at renewal. Outside the renewal window, the duplicate-card cost applies.
transfer_summary: A new resident applies for a Wisconsin license within 60 days of establishing residence. A commercial license has a shorter deadline.
teen_summary: An instruction permit is the first step, and a probationary license follows a driving skills test. Passenger and night limits apply until the graduated restrictions end.
out_of_state_permit: A teen moving to Wisconsin may take one road test on a valid out-of-state learner's permit, or one expired less than one year, at age 16, and must show driver education.
curfew: From midnight to 5 a.m., a probationary driver may drive alone only between home, school, and work. Other trips need a parent, guardian, or another qualified licensed person in the front seat.
passengers: A probationary driver may drive with immediate family and only one other passenger, or with a qualified adult.

transfer_points.heading: What happens at the exam station
transfer_points.label: First Wyoming license
transfer_points.text: You apply in person at a local driver exam station. You can start the process on oneWYO. You will be asked to surrender your out-of-state issued driver license when you apply for the Wyoming license, present the required document requirements, be photographed, and complete a vision screening evaluation.
